preamble: The Across solutions are thematic; their clues lack thematic definitions.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: overturned tells us to turn the word for cask upside down, reading it backwards in this down clue

parts.note: a butt is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A bathhouse equipped with a cask that has been tipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' turns BUTT into TTUB, which follows HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a large heated outdoor tub people soak in, a kind of bath.

indicators.note: modified signals that the spelt-out time is rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the time three-ten, spelt out as the words three and ten

explanation.surface: A computer network has a 3.10 update installed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read '3.10' as the words THREE TEN; 'modified' rearranges those eight letters. The surface suggests a software version number.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethernet is the common wired system linking computers in a local area network.

clue.text: Wizard's lean description of a honeycomb?

parts.note: a hex is a witch or wizard (Pennsylvania Dutch usage), and Wizard's is read as wizard is
lean, as of a bony figure, means angular

explanation.surface: A thin wizard is being described, perhaps in a story about bees.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: honeycomb cells are six-sided.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeycomb cells are six-sided, so a honeycomb could be called six-cornered, the meaning of this adjective.

clue.text: Where work is a grind on motorway with learners

parts.note: motorway gives MI
L is the learner plate letter, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: Learner drivers on the motorway find it hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, learner drivers display L plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill grinds grain, and the word also names any place of dreary, relentless toil.

clue.text: They pass judgment having forwarded new screen

parts.note: to have forwarded a message is to have sent it on

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of screen are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Critics pass judgment after a new screen has been sent to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SCREEN into ENCERS, which follows SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Judges who hand down punishments to convicted people pass sentence, which is passing judgment.

indicators.note: In signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters across torpid and lethargy

explanation.surface: Someone lies in a torpid, lethargic state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' indicates the hidden run spanning torpID LEthargy, and the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sluggish and inactive is being lazy and unoccupied, so the whole phrase describes it.

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners
to rest is to remain, as in rest assured

explanation.surface: The artillerymen staying behind are the finest of the lot.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is a common crossword abbreviation for gunners.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare can mean exceptionally good, so the superlative means the finest of all.

indicators.note: in signals that the parking letter and the woman go inside the outhouse word

parts.note: a shed is an outbuilding or outhouse
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
her is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: A clergyman leaves a woman's car in an outhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P and HER inside SHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor tends a flock of believers, and the word for a sheep-keeper is used figuratively of a minister.

indicators.note: edited signals that the letters of the phrase are rewritten into a different order

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline was left unchanged by the editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edited' rearranges all fourteen letters of THE HEADLINE NOT. The title is an Agatha Christie novel; the theme is novels.
explanation.definitionFit: This Agatha Christie mystery set aboard a river steamer in Egypt is one of the theme's novels.

clue.text: Lapse into sin in season in Vermont

explanation.surface: Someone backslides during autumn in New England.
explanation.walkthrough: Americans call autumn the fall; the first sense is the biblical one. The title is also a novel by Albert Camus.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve's first disobedience is mankind's original slip from grace, while autumn is called by this name in American English.

clue.text: You once took in some French priest

indicators.note: took in means the old word for you encloses the French word

parts.note: thee is the archaic form of you
de is French for some or of, as in du and de la

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person once welcomed a French cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took in' puts DE inside THEE, and P follows. The title is a Peter Benchley novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Benchley's underwater treasure-hunting thriller is one of the theme's novels.

clue.text: Scottish mountain with obstacle. Not half

parts.note: ben is the Scots word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

indicators.note: Not half means only half of the word for obstacle is kept, the second three letters dropped

parts.note: a hurdle is an obstacle to be jumped

explanation.surface: A Scottish peak presents a barrier, though not a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' removes DLE, keeping HUR. The title is Lew Wallace's novel of chariot racing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lew Wallace's tale of a Judean prince and a chariot race is one of the theme's novels.

indicators.note: developed, as photographs are, signals the letters being worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A photographic enlargement has been developed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges ENLARGEMENT. The title is a John Buchan spy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: John Buchan's First World War Richard Hannay adventure is one of the theme's novels.

clue.text: Timeless problems about rent, reviewed for US inhabitants

indicators.note: about means the shortened problems word goes around the rearranged rent
Timeless tells us to drop the letter standing for time from the word for problems

parts.note: teasers are puzzling problems

indicators.note: reviewed signals that the letters of rent are viewed again in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Problems with rent are being reviewed for Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' drops T from TEASERS to leave EASERS; 'reviewed' turns RENT into TERN; 'about' puts EASERS round TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the eastern states, such as New England, are so called by other Americans.

explanation.walkthrough: Go means energy or liveliness, so the plural of the word for liveliness can be read from 'Go's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Animation means vivacity or go, and it also means moving images drawn or generated by computer.

clue.text: Impetuous folk placing articles in scuttles

indicators.note: in means the two articles are put inside the scuttles word

parts.note: a hod, like a coal scuttle, is a container for carrying coal
the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Rash people are putting goods into coal buckets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives both THE and A, which go inside HODS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash, quick-tempered person acts on impulse, so impetuous folk fit the plural.

indicators.note: In signals the answer lies within the letters of summer's heat

explanation.surface: It is hot in the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are hidden across summer'S HEat. The title is H. Rider Haggard's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard's adventure about an immortal African queen is one of the theme's novels.

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for independent, as of a politician

indicators.note: returned signals that the parliament's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: An independent candidate was elected back to parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns DAIL into LIAD, after I. Homer's epic poem is the theme entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic of the Trojan War stands among the theme's great narrative works.

clue.text: Gas masks from popular callers, reportedly

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word for callers is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: hailers are people who call out to others

explanation.surface: Gas masks come from people who are popular with visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: HAILERS sounds the same as HALERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A device breathed through to take in vapour or medication is a kind of mask for gas.

indicators.note: during means the scrambled hero sits inside the word for meal

parts.note: tea is an evening meal in Britain

indicators.note: drunk signals that the letters of Hercules are scrambled

explanation.surface: Hercules got drunk during a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges HERCULES into HECRULES, and 'during' puts it inside TEA. The title is Nicholas Monsarrat's naval novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Monsarrat's novel of the Battle of the Atlantic is one of the theme's novels.

parts.note: even and yet both intensify, as in even better and yet better

indicators.note: half means only one of the two halves of the word only is kept, the first two letters going

explanation.surface: Something is done evenly, though only halfway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps LY from ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a regular, consistent manner throughout is doing it smoothly and level.

indicators.note: suggested indicates a word that is only hinted at by sound, not spelling

parts.note: rime is hoar frost, and the plural is read from Frost's

explanation.surface: Robert Frost's poems are hinted at as jingles.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the poet Robert Frost, but frost is rime.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple jingles are short verses that chime at line ends.

indicators.note: backing signals that the contracted we are is read in reverse

parts.note: we are contracts to we're, spelt WERE without its apostrophe
Hon is short for Honourable, the title of a dignitary

explanation.surface: We support an important person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns WERE into EREW. The title is Samuel Butler's satire, nearly nowhere reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler's satirical novel about an imaginary land is one of the theme's novels.

explanation.walkthrough: Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine; it is also the ankle joint of an animal's hind leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhenish white wine is called this in Britain, and the tarsal joint in a horse's hind leg has the same name.

clue.text: Temple's quiet — one right by meadow

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
I is the Roman numeral one
a ley is a meadow or grassland

explanation.surface: Shirley Temple, the child star, was quiet in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temple' evokes the child star Shirley Temple. The title is Charlotte Bronte's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Bronte's novel of the Yorkshire Luddite riots is one of the theme's novels.

indicators.note: away signals that the miles letter is removed from the river's name

parts.note: the Somme is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: A small river is a few miles off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes one M from SOMME.
explanation.definitionFit: Some means a modest amount, as in have some cake.

indicators.note: in means the words for some and railway go inside the capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
any means some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: Some people travelled by rail in the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ANY and RY inside ROME. The title is George Borrow's novel of Gypsy life.
explanation.definitionFit: George Borrow's sequel to Lavengro about travelling people is one of the theme's novels.
